excluded_fields.reason: resolvable slugs, not prose — a stub_id containing 'scope' would trip the token leg on every scan

legs.description: An explicitly PM-prefixed gate string. The one leg that is unambiguous by construction — the author wrote the prefix to mean exactly this.

mechanical_floor.note: Fleet-stable ROLE words only. This is a floor, not the leg.

legs.description: Who a gate is addressed to is not derivable by matching. A stakeholder is often a peer TEAM rather than a role word -- 'coordinate with claude-klabauter-em', 'ask whoever owns the ingest path' -- and resolving that takes knowledge of the fleet and of who is actually on the hook, which no term list holds. The mechanical floor catches the role words; everything past it is EM judgment and surfaces as a judgment point offering the candidate, never as a silent yes or no. A consumer that implements only the floor and reports the leg as done has closed a judgment call by omission.
legs.never: Do not extend the floor into peer-team or person names -- neither a hardcoded roster nor an inferred one. A fleet roster decays the moment a repo is added or renamed, and the wrong answer here is invisible: a gate silently addressed to nobody.

legs.description: Product-coupling tokens. 'policy' and 'scope' are deliberately high-recall and low-precision — 'out of scope' is common prose. They earn their place because a missed PM gate blocks a roadmap close at Audit 3, while an over-fired row costs the author one dismissal.
User-visible-behaviour language. Product direction by definition, so it surfaces regardless of who authored the stub.

row_template.authored_by: the EM, not the detector — the detector recommends the stub_id; the gate question is authored content

cross_check.note: Audit 3: every stub with a 'PM '-prefixed gate has a pm-gates.md row referencing its stub_id. Audit 4: every pending row is referenced by at least one stub. Mismatch blocks Phase 2 close with exit 1. A detector that emits a row without the stub referencing it back therefore breaks close in the other direction.
